recommendation: Run the nightly day-ahead forecast and use it to plan rebalancing before the commuter peaks
evidence: Working-day rush hours (07-09 and 16-19) hold 58% of working-day rentals; peaks of 477/h (08:00) and 525/h (17:00). Forecast WAPE 19.5% vs 24.3% for the best simple method
expected_benefit: 20% lower hourly error than the best simple baseline (13%-26% 95% CI) and 41% lower than 'same hour last week'
kpi: Forecast WAPE; empty-bike and full-dock incidents at peak

recommendation: Plan fleet buffers from the calibrated 80% interval, not the point forecast
evidence: Real coverage of the interval is 75% (nominal 80%), whereas a naive Poisson interval covers only 33%; the average upper bound sits 153 bikes/h above the forecast at commuter peaks
expected_benefit: About 89% of hours stay at or below the upper bound, giving a quantified safety margin
kpi: Interval coverage; share of peak hours above the upper bound

recommendation: Make operations weather-aware: scale deployed fleet and crew plans with the forecast
evidence: At the same hour and season, +10 C raises rentals 28%, light rain/snow cuts them 40%, +10 km/h wind cuts them 3%; weather information lowers forecast error from 52 to 43 bikes/h
expected_benefit: Fewer idle bikes on cold or wet days, more bikes on warm days
kpi: Utilisation per bike by weather class

recommendation: Schedule maintenance and large rebalancing runs in the 00:00-05:59 window
evidence: Only 3.2% of all rentals occur between midnight and 06:00

recommendation: Treat weekends as a different product: keep fleet size but shift bikes to leisure areas and promote casual use at midday
evidence: Daily totals are similar on working and non-working days (about 4,585 vs 4,390), but weekends have a single midday peak (380/h at 13:00) and a 32% casual share vs 13% on working days
expected_benefit: Better placement and conversion of casual riders

recommendation: Add holiday-period and severe-weather rules: flag the days around public holidays, and do not rely on the model during extreme events
evidence: 6 of the 8 worst-forecast days are within one day of a public holiday (e.g. the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve), and WAPE on holiday-adjacent days is 42% against 17% on other days; rain/snow hours have WAPE 43% vs 17% in clear weather; Hurricane Sandy shut the system down (most hours of 29-30 Oct were never recorded)
expected_benefit: Avoids acting on forecasts at the times they are known to fail
kpi: Forecast error on flagged days; number of manual overrides

recommendation: Retrain monthly and monitor forecast bias and WAPE to handle growth
evidence: Demand grew 63% per hour from 2011 to 2012; the level-adjusted design copes with growth, but forecast errors are autocorrelated (lag-24 ACF 0.30), so level drift must be monitored

recommendation: Invest in better data: station-level trips, bike availability, real weather forecasts and an events calendar
evidence: Forecast-quality weather instead of perfect weather raises MAE by about 4%; observed rentals understate true demand when bikes run out
expected_benefit: Station-level rebalancing and less hidden (unserved) demand
kpi: Share of demand served; station-level forecast error
